notes:
CIRCUIT: a three-rail ladder. Top rail y~272 (x=115..830), middle rail y~450 (x~40..935), bottom rail y~672 (x=115..850), joined by five vertical columns at x = 115, 372, 512, 685, 849; each column carries one two-terminal part above the middle rail and one below. Series elements sit in the rails themselves. 18 components, 12 nets. Ground appears once, under the 2k resistor at the far right.

NET MAP
  n3  = top rail left of the top inductor: V-AC #2 top lead + L #1 left lead (x=115..197, y~275).
  n1  = top rail centre: L #1 right lead + top lead of Zener #4 (T at (361,275)) + top lead of Diode #6 (T at (499,275)) + left plate of C #0 (15uF) at (550,271).
  n2  = top rail right: right plate of C #0 + top lead of Zener #3 (T at (670,274)) + top lead of Diode #5 (the rail corners down at x~830 into the x=849 column).
  n4  = middle rail left: V-AC #2 bottom lead + I-DC #9 top lead (4-way dot at (112,462)) + bottom lead of Zener #4 + left plate of C #7 (9uF) + top lead of Diode #13 (4-way dot at (365,455)). This net also owns the un-annotated capacitor glyph at x~30..45 at the left end of the rail (see UNRESOLVED).
  n5  = middle rail centre: right plate of C #7 + bottom lead of Zener #3 + top lead of Diode #14 (4-way dot at (681,446)) + LEFT lead of L #8 (4uH). Passes OVER the x=512 column at (511,450) without joining it.
  n8  = middle rail right of L #8: right lead of L #8 + top lead of R #10 (2k). Passes OVER the x=849 column at (849,445) without joining it.
  n7  = the floating midpoint of the x=512 column: bottom lead of Diode #6 + top lead of Zener #12. Two terminals only, by the S20 crossing decision.
  n6  = the floating midpoint of the x=849 column: bottom lead of Diode #5 + top lead of Diode #11. Two terminals only, by the S18 crossing decision.
  n9  = bottom rail left: I-DC #9 bottom lead + left plate of C #16 (x=115..196, y~673).
  n11 = bottom rail centre: right plate of C #16 + bottom lead of Diode #13 (dot at (380,674)) + bottom lead of Zener #12 (dot at (518,674)) + left lead of L #17 (4uH).
  n10 = bottom rail right: right lead of L #17 + bottom lead of Diode #14 (dot at (709,671)) + bottom lead of Diode #11 (the rail corners up at x~850 into the column).
  0   = R #10 bottom lead + GND #15. Two terminals; the only ground in the drawing.

SITE DECISIONS
  The drafter of this sheet marks EVERY intended connection with a deliberate hand-scribbled solder circle. All six T-junctions (S4 (499,275) dot=2.1, S5 (670,274) 2.5, S7 (361,275) 2.1, S44 (709,671) 2.5, S47 (380,674) 2.5, S48 (518,674) 2.9) carry one, and three of the five middle-rail 4-way crossings carry one (S24 (112,462) 2.5, S21 (365,455) 2.5, S17 (681,446) 2.8). Verified in the pixels: at S17 the blob is a closed ~17x11 px loop against a 2-3 px stroke, i.e. the drafter literally drew a small filled circle. Those nine are recorded as junction.
  S18 (849,445) OVERRIDDEN to crossing. At 12x zoom this is a bare X: four 2-3 px arms meeting with zero thickening (dot score 1.8, no hop). The left rail stroke sits at y=446-448 and the right one at y=444-445, so the rail was drawn as two overlapping passes, but there is no blob of any kind. Consequence of the other reading: n8 and n6 would merge into a single 4-terminal node {L#8 right, R#10 top, D#5 bottom, D#11 top} and the net count would drop to 11. I rejected it because the same drafter drew an obvious circle at the three comparable middle-rail crossings on the same rail (S17/S21/S24) and at every T; leaving two of them bare twice is a deliberate distinction, not an omission. Both readings are electrically sane (crossing leaves D#5+D#11 as an ordinary series pair between the top and bottom rails with a floating midpoint), so rule 1 does not decide it and the drafter's own habit does.
  S20 (511,450) OVERRIDDEN to crossing, same argument (dot score 1.6). At 12x zoom the horizontal rail steps from y=451-452 to y=449-450 right at the column and there is a small 7x5 px stroke-overlap lump at (501,450), i.e. 10 px LEFT of the crossing and only ~2x stroke width - nothing like the 15-17 px circles at S17/S21/S24. Consequence of the other reading: n7 would merge into n5, giving a 6-terminal middle node and 11 nets. Rejected for the same reason.
  Non-critical sites S0, S2, S3, S8-S11, S13, S15, S16, S23, S25-S28, S32-S35, S37, S38, S40, S42, S43 are all handwriting ('15uF', '9uF', '4uH', '8V', '1kHz', '3A', '5V', '2kOhm') or symbol ink brushing a wire; defaults left alone. S23 (53,461) is the un-annotated capacitor glyph at the left end of the middle rail.

PORT / PIN FIXES (four terminals had landed on handwriting, each producing a one-terminal net)
  #0 Capacitor t0: was p3@(579,239), a stroke of '15uF'. Moved to p1@(550,271), the real left plate lead.
  #2 V-AC t1: was p1@(165,375), a stroke of '1kHz'. Moved to p5@(112,301), the real top lead (wire id 105, the same wire as inductor #1's left lead).
  #4 Zener t1: was p2@(405,344), a stroke of '5V'. Moved to p1@(361,312), the real top lead.
  #9 I-DC t1: was p2@(166,577), a stroke of '3A'. Moved to p1@(113,492), the real top lead.
  #8 Inductor t0: the tracer found NO port candidate on the left side of the box at all - its only left-ish candidates (p1..p4) are strokes of the '4uH' label below. The left lead wire does exist: edge e49 runs from (728,446) to (686,447), i.e. from 9 px outside the box edge (x=737) back to the S17 dot. I cleared t0's port and pinned it with manual_nets 8.0 = n5, the middle-rail-centre net that e49 belongs to. Verified in the pixels and in the #8 crop that the rail enters the coil from the left.
  No 3-terminal parts in this drawing, so no pin-order work. Diode/zener terminal order left at the tracer default (order is not scored for 2-terminal parts).

CLASSES: all 18 agree with the drawing. The three symbols the inventory calls Zener Diode (#3 at (667,338), #4 at (365,343), #12 at (516,550)) are exactly the three drawn with a bent-end cathode bar and are exactly the three annotated '5V'; the five plain-bar triangles are Diodes.

UNRESOLVED / NOTED: there is a clearly drawn capacitor glyph (two parallel plates at x~27 and x~43, y~440-478) at the extreme left end of the middle rail that is NOT in the published component inventory. Its left plate has no wire at all - the ink stops there. I did not add a component (the brief forbids changing the inventory), and it does not affect any net: the rail ink there is part of n4 and no annotated terminal touches it. If the inventory is ever corrected, that part would be a Capacitor with one lead on n4 and one lead unconnected.

=== SECOND READER (audit pass) ===
CHANGED: S18 (849,445) and S20 (511,450), both CROSSING -> JUNCTION. Net count
12 -> 10. Nothing else changed: the port fixes, manual_nets 8.0=n5 (still the
correct label after the merge - the middle-rail-centre net is still emitted as
n5), the nine dotted junctions and the un-annotated capacitor glyph note all
stand.

Consequence: the first pass's two "floating column midpoints" disappear.
  n7 {D#6 bottom, Z#12 top}  is absorbed into the middle-rail-centre net, which
     becomes {C#7 right, D#6 bottom, Z#3 bottom, Z#12 top, D#14 top, L#8 left}
     = 6 terminals.
  n6 {D#5 bottom, D#11 top}  is absorbed into the middle-rail-right net, which
     becomes {L#8 right, D#5 bottom, D#11 top, R#10 top} = 4 terminals.
So all five columns join all three rails, i.e. this is a plain full ladder.

WHY (evidence the first pass did not use):
1. EXACT GRAPH ISOMORPHISM WITH ALL THREE VERIFIED SIBLINGS. Testing the
   component-class-labelled netlist graph against circuit_350, circuit_748 and
   circuit_856 (all human-verified, all 10 nets):
       as-is (12 nets)      -> isomorphic to none
       S20=junction only    -> isomorphic to none
       S18=junction only    -> isomorphic to none
       BOTH junctions       -> isomorphic to ALL THREE
   The match is not just the net-count or the size multiset
   ([2,2,2,3,3,4,4,4,5,6]); it is column-by-column. Against circuit_856:
   col1 V-AC/I-DC, col2 Zener/Diode, col3 Diode/Zener, col4 Zener/Diode,
   col5 Diode/Diode; top rail Inductor(col1|col2) + Capacitor(col2|col3);
   middle rail Capacitor(col2|col3) + Inductor(col4|col5); bottom rail
   Capacitor(col1|col2) + Inductor(col3|col4); Resistor+GND hanging off the
   middle rail's right end. circuit_896 reproduces every one of those
   positions. Three independent drafters drawing the same generated circuit do
   not all coincide on a topology that differs from this sheet by exactly the
   two contested nodes.
2. SIBLING LAYOUT. circuit_856 is the same three-rail / five-column ladder
   drawn in the same orientation, and there every column meets every rail
   (its middle-rail nodes at x~290, 465, 620, 795 are all dotted junctions).
   The generated circuit has no floating column midpoint anywhere.
3. NO "NOT CONNECTED" MARK AT EITHER SITE. Neither is a hop and neither is a
   jog. The x=849 column runs x=847@y=398 -> 849@y=442 -> 849@y=459 ->
   853@y=516: a steady ~1px/15px rightward pen drift with NO step at the rail.
   The x=511 column runs 510@y=443 -> 511@y=447 -> 511@y=453 -> 515@y=519:
   same steady drift, no step. The comparable dotted junction S21 shows the
   same drift (365 above, 366-368 below), so the drift is this pen, not a jog.
   Nowhere on this sheet does the drafter draw a hop - because in a full
   ladder nothing ever needs to cross, which is exactly the point.
4. The generic ink prior also points to junction: a bare X with no dot and no
   hop resolves junction about 2:1 across the verified set (measured: 53
   junction / 27 crossing over 60 cal sheets).

WHAT THE FIRST PASS SAW IS REAL BUT IS AN OMISSION, NOT A DISTINCTION. The
solder circles at S17/S21/S24 really are ~15-17px closed loops and neither
contested site has one; S20 has only a ~13x4px smear at (498-511,448-451),
i.e. a flat stroke-overlap lump 8px left of the column, and S18 has no blob at
all. But two missed dots out of eleven junctions on a hand sheet is ordinary
sloppiness, whereas the crossing reading requires the drafter to have invented
two floating column midpoints that no other drawing of this circuit has and to
have marked neither of them with the hop he uses nowhere else. The dot habit is
weaker evidence than three independent verified drawings agreeing.
